title: Replace Draw's Bespoke UtilityStateMachine With Shared Fsm Crate
description: D2: draw/plugin/rs/lib.rs hand-rolls a pointer-gesture state machine (DrawDragState enum: Marquee/Shape/Draft, driven from canvasPointerDown/Move/Up/canvasDoubleClick/canvasCommitDraft/canvasEscape/SET_ACTIVE_UTILITY_ACTION_ID action arms). Replace it with the shared fsm crate's statechart! DSL (fsm/rs, fsm/macros/rs) — map draw's states/events onto the fsm vocabulary (Machine/Snapshot/Command/CommandSink), keep only the minimal document-touching commit logic (hit-testing, marquee/shape/draft commit, trace) as host-side effect handlers since fsm's ActionFn/GuardFn only get (&mut Context, Option&Event) and have no access to the DrawDocument tree. Delete the old DrawDragState enum and its ad-hoc match-based transition logic once fsm fully drives it. Investigate imperative/engine/rs too (per instructions) — expected to be irrelevant (it's a headless step/path script executor, not a UI gesture FSM) but confirm before ruling it out. Flag any genuine fsm capability gaps instead of hacking around them. Keep C1-C7 conformance intact.
summary: Replaced draw's hand-rolled DrawDragState enum + inline match-based pointer-gesture transition ladder with the shared fsm crate's statechart! DSL. draw-plugin now depends on `fsm` (fsm/rs, default features: macros+serde) and declares a `draw_gesture` machine (states idle/marqueeing/shape_dragging/drafting; events PointerDown/PointerMove/PointerUp/CommitDraft/Escape/UtilityChanged) compiled to fsm's dense static NodeDef/TransitionDef tables. DrawPlayApp now carries a live `draw_gesture::Snapshot` (via fsm::init/fsm::macrostep) alongside the trimmed DrawInteractionState (selected_ids/hovered_id/engagement_input only, `drag` field removed). Investigated imperative/engine/rs per instructions and confirmed it is unrelated (headless Step/Path side-effect script executor, no gesture/UI-state vocabulary) — not used. No changes made to fsm/rs or fsm/macros/rs; the existing DSL's guard/action/effect vocabulary was sufficient without any additive API. All document-touching logic (hit-testing, marquee/shape/draft commit, trace) is unchanged and now runs from a new `DrawPlayApp::step_gesture` host-side effect dispatcher (fsm's ActionFn/GuardFn only see Context+Event, never the DrawDocument tree — this is the one documented capability boundary, handled by threading a GestureEffect enum through Command::Effect rather than forcing document access into fsm actions). Verified: full manual cross-reference of every guard/action/state/target identifier used in the statechart! block against its Rust definition (script-checked, zero missing), brace/paren/bracket balance across the whole file, and `rustfmt --check` with the repo's rustfmt.toml producing zero syntax errors (only the same pre-existing width-driven diff noise present in the untouched original file, confirmed by diffing counts against the pre-edit backup: 51 vs 52 sections, i.e. no new formatting surface). `cargo check -p draw-plugin --lib` was started twice but never completed within the session — the shared target/ dir is under heavy contention from many other concurrent sessions' cargo processes (confirmed via ps aux showing 15+ concurrent cargo check/rustc invocations queued on the same lock); left running in the background for the orchestrator's final workspace-wide gate. No test file changes were needed: all existing draw-plugin tests drive the machine exclusively through the public handle_action/render API (none referenced DrawDragState/interaction.drag directly), so behavior parity rests on the 1:1 mapping documented in the guard/action functions.
